In [[mathematics]], '''Tate duality''' or '''Poitou–Tate duality''' is a duality theorem for [[Galois cohomology]] groups of modules over the [[Galois group]] of an [[algebraic number field]] or [[local field]], introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Tate|first=John|author-link=John Tate (mathematician)|year=1962}} and {{harvs|txt|last=Poitou|first=Georges|author-link=Georges Poitou|year=1967}}.

==Local Tate duality==

{{main|local Tate duality}}
For a ''p''-adic local field <math>k</math>, local Tate duality says there is a [[perfect pairing]] of the [[finite group]]s arising from Galois cohomology:
:<math>\displaystyle H^r(k,M)\times H^{2-r}(k,M')\rightarrow H^2(k,\mathbb{G}_m)=\Q/ \Z</math>
where <math>M</math> is a finite group scheme, <math>M'</math> its dual <math>\operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathbb{G}_m)</math>, and <math>\mathbb{G}_m</math> is the [[multiplicative group]].
For a local field of characteristic <math>p>0</math>, the statement is similar, except that the pairing takes values in <math>H^2(k, \mu) = \bigcup_{p \nmid n} \tfrac{1}{n} \Z/\Z</math>.<ref>{{harvtxt|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2000|loc=Theorem 7.2.6}}</ref> The statement also holds when <math>k</math> is an [[Archimedean field]], though the definition of the cohomology groups looks somewhat different in this case.

==Global Tate duality==
Given a finite group scheme <math>M</math> over a global field <math>k</math>, global Tate duality relates the cohomology of <math>M</math> with that of <math>M' = \operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathbb{G}_m)</math> using the local pairings constructed above. This is done via the localization maps
:<math> \alpha_{r, M}: H^r(k, M) \rightarrow {\prod_v}' H^r(k_v, M), </math>
where <math>v</math> varies over all places of <math>k</math>, and where <math>\prod'</math> denotes a restricted product with respect to the unramified cohomology groups. Summing the local pairings gives a canonical perfect pairing
:<math>{\prod_v}' H^r(k_v, M) \times {\prod_v}' H^{2- r}(k_v, M') \rightarrow \Q/\Z .</math>
One part of Poitou-Tate duality states that, under this pairing, the image of <math>H^r(k, M)</math> has annihilator equal to the image of <math>H^{2-r}(k, M')</math> for <math> r = 0, 1, 2</math>.

The map <math>\alpha_{r, M}</math> has a finite kernel for all <math>r</math>, and Tate also constructs a canonical perfect pairing
:<math> \text{ker}(\alpha_{1, M}) \times \ker(\alpha_{2, M'}) \rightarrow \Q/\Z .</math>

These dualities are often presented in the form of a nine-term exact sequence
:<math> 0 \rightarrow H^0(k, M) \rightarrow {\prod_v}' H^0(k_v, M) \rightarrow  H^2(k, M')^* </math>
:<math> \rightarrow H^1(k, M) \rightarrow {\prod_v}' H^1(k_v, M) \rightarrow H^1(k, M')^*</math>
:<math> \rightarrow H^2(k, M) \rightarrow {\prod_v}' H^2(k_v, M) \rightarrow H^0(k, M')^* \rightarrow 0.</math>
Here, the asterisk denotes the Pontryagin dual of a given locally compact abelian group.

All of these statements were presented by Tate in a more general form depending on a set of places <math> S</math> of <math>k</math>, with the above statements being the form of his theorems for the case where <math>S</math> contains all places of <math>k</math>. For the more general result, see e.g.
{{harvtxt|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2000|loc=Theorem 8.4.4}}.

==Poitou–Tate duality==
Among other statements, Poitou–Tate duality establishes a perfect pairing between certain [[Shafarevich group]]s. Given a global field <math>k</math>, a set ''S'' of primes, and the maximal extension <math>k_S</math> which is unramified outside ''S'', the Shafarevich groups capture, broadly speaking, those elements in the cohomology of <math>\operatorname{Gal}(k_S/k)</math> which vanish in the Galois cohomology of the local fields pertaining to the primes in ''S''.<ref>See {{harvtxt|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2000|loc=Theorem 8.6.8}} for a precise statement.</ref>

An extension to the case where the ring of ''S''-integers <math>\mathcal{O}_S</math> is replaced by a regular scheme of finite type over <math>\operatorname{Spec} \mathcal{O}_S</math> was shown by {{harvtxt|Geisser|Schmidt|2018}}. Another generalisation is due to Česnavičius, who relaxed the condition on the localising set ''S'' by using [[flat cohomology]] on smooth proper curves.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Česnavičius |first=Kęstutis |date=2015 |title=Poitou–Tate without restrictions on the order |url=https://www.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/2015/0022/0006/MRL-2015-0022-0006-a005.pdf |journal=[[Mathematical Research Letters]] |volume=22 |issue=6 |pages=1621–1666|doi=10.4310/MRL.2015.v22.n6.a5 }}</ref>
